**[#8527](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/8527) — pragma once is case sensitive**  
<sub>batch 004 · triaged against `eff900d5` · drafted by `claude-opus-5 (Copilot CLI)` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol`</sub>

Reproduces on main (1.9.0.15422, eff900d54) and on every release v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607; not a regression. Title understates it: not case folding -- #pragma once is keyed on the path AS SPELLED, so './x.hlsli' vs 'x.hlsli' fails identically with the case held constant. DxcArgsFileSystemImpl::TryFindOrOpen matches includes by wcscmp on the spelled name and GetFileInformationByHandle reports the slot handle as the file index, so FileManager's UniqueID dedup sees two files. Matching-case control compiles clean; #ifndef guards are an effective workaround. Measured on Windows/NTFS only. No CE link: multi-file repro, and the single-file fold measures clang's pragma-once-in-main-file rule instead.

> ⚠️ **Issue text is stale.** Title says 'case sensitive'. Case is not the mechanism: #pragma once keys on the path as spelled, so './x' vs '././x' fails with case held constant. The real scope is wider than the title.

*Labels:* add `usability`, `check-in-clang`; remove `needs-triage`.

*No Compiler Explorer link:* no valid single-file demonstration exists. The repro needs a header plus two includers and CE is single-file; CE also runs Linux, where the reported case-mismatched name does not exist. The obvious fold -- a file including itself under a different spelling of its own path -- was built, run on CE and REJECTED: the identical construction with a matching spelling fails the same way, so it measures clang's documented 'pragma once is ignored in the main file' rule, not this defect. Evidence: manual-case-godbolt.txt, variant-selfinclude-samespelling-main-debug.txt.

**[#8737](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/8737) — Atomics on RWTexture2DMS result in silent UB or ICE**  
<sub>batch 004 · triaged against `eff900d5` · drafted by `claude-opus-5 (Copilot CLI)` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol`</sub>

Both reported symptoms confirmed on main (eff900d54) and on every SM 6.7-capable release since v1.7.2207. ICE: InterlockedMax(tex.sample[s][uv],..) exits E_FAIL with 'llvm::cast<X>() argument of incompatible type!' (a thrown hlsl::Exception, identical in Debug and Release); also fires with a constant sample index, other atomics and RWTexture2DMSArray. Silent case: compiles with exit 0 and no diagnostic, emitting dx.op.atomicBinOp with 'i32 undef' in the last coordinate on a 2dMS UAV -- byte-identical to the same atomic on a plain RWTexture2D. DXIL.rst:1876-1887 does not list Texture2DMS among AtomicBinOp's valid resource types and gen_intrin_main.txt declares no interlocked method on RWTexture2DMS, so this is invalid input DXC fails to diagnose, not valid input it miscompiles. The validator does not catch it either (DxilValidation.cpp:2412 checks UAV-ness, not resource kind).

> ⚠️ **Issue text is stale.** Title says 'silent UB or ICE'; understates it. The silent case emits a DXIL atomic with i32 undef where the sample index belongs, and that container passes validation.

**[#2202](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/2202) — Validation error "DXIL intrinsic overload must be valid"**  
<sub>batch 004 · triaged against `eff900d5` · drafted by `claude-opus-5` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol`</sub>

Repros on main (eff900d5) and every release v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607. Must be compiled -HV 2018: at today's default -HV 2021 the front end rejects the vector-condition '?:' before codegen, so the validator never runs and it falsely looks fixed. -Vd shows codegen, not the validator, is at fault: the compile succeeds and emits 'call double @dx.op.dot3.f64', but hctdb declares Dot3 with overloads 'hf' (half/float only), so the validator is correct and -Vd just yields DXIL no runtime accepts. Literal-float ternary resolves to double; HLSL declares dot over 'numeric' (includes double), DXIL cannot express it. FXC compiles the same source in float. The reporter's second ask (no line number) was fixed in v1.6.2104. Same DXIL-level gap as open #8208 (mul on double4 -> dot4.f64).

*Labels:* add `type-system`, `fxc-disagrees`, `diagnostic`.

Derived-to-base conversion crashes codegen (LLVM assert, 0xE0000001, in CGMSHLSLRuntime::ConvertAndStoreElements). Reproduces in all 20 releases v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607.

*Labels:* add `type-system`; remove `check-in-clang`.

**[#3873](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/3873) — Infinite loop related to struct inheritance and empty struct**  
<sub>batch 002 · triaged against `eff900d5` · drafted by `claude-opus-5 (Copilot CLI)` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol`</sub>

Empty-struct inheritance hangs the compiler. Release builds spin unbounded (still running at 300s); Debug builds trip an LLVM assert in ~2s on the same input. Reproduces v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607 at ps_6_0.

*Labels:* add `type-system`.


## Provenance and limits

- Ground truth is a **Debug** build of `main` (2 commits across batches). Debug matters: many older issues are asserts, which a Release build compiles out.
- **The release bisection floor is v1.4.1907** (2019-07), the oldest release shipping a usable `dxc`. For issues filed before it, "always reproduced" means "for as long as it is possible to check". SPIR-V issues have a higher floor still.
- **Compiler Explorer runs Release builds**, so a Debug-only assert looks clean there. CE corroborates the local build; it never overrules it. `dxc_trunk` is a rolling build and is not reproducible over time.
- **Sampling is deliberately unrepresentative.** Batches over-weight the oldest issues, so the verdict distribution here does not generalise to the backlog.

Per-batch reports, including the method findings that changed how later batches were run: [batch 001](batch-001.md), [batch 002](batch-002.md), [batch 003](batch-003.md), [batch 004](batch-004.md).
